abstract: Phosphorylation of the C-terminal domain (CTD) of RNA polymerase II (Pol II) by the cyclin-dependent kinase C (CDKC)-CYCT complex is crucial for Pol II-mediated transcription in Arabidopsis. Here, we show that phase separation of the intrinsically disordered protein EMBRYO DEFECTIVE 1579 (EMB1579) orchestrates this process. CDKC;2, the major CDKC family protein in Arabidopsis, interacts with EMB1579 at least in part through its C-terminal intrinsically disordered region (IDR), and the two proteins co-condense in vitro, with EMB1579 acting as the primary driver of condensate formation. In vivo, CDKC;2 colocalizes with EMB1579 condensates, and EMB1579 phase separation enhances CDKC;2-mediated CTD phosphorylation both in vitro and in planta. Strikingly, EMB1579 condensates recruit not only CDKC;2 but also CYCT and synthetic CTD peptides, functioning as reaction hubs for Pol II CTD phosphorylation. This study reveals a novel mechanism by which phase-separated biomolecular condensates spatially organize transcriptional kinases to precisely regulate Pol II activity, advancing our understanding of eukaryotic transcription regulation.
